chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who buys foodstuff, then sells it before he takes possession of it. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem. And if the man appoints the buyer from him to take possession of it and measure it, he said: There is no problem (with that).

key_terms.يُوَكِّلُ: To appoint as an agent / delegate

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell food before taking possession of it in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of selling foodstuff before physical possession (qabd), a foundational principle in Shia commercial jurisprudence that facilitates trade by reducing transaction friction. It further validates the delegation of possession and measurement to an agent, reflecting the practical needs of market transactions in early Islamic society. This ruling aligns with the broader Shia view that 'qabd' refers to constructive or effective possession rather than strictly immediate physical handling, provided the goods are distinct and measurable.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Hadeed, from Jameel Bin Darraj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

regarding the man who buys the foodstuff, then sells it before he takes possession of it’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’. (I said), ‘Can the buyer from him appoint the man (another one) to take possession of it and have it measured?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem (with that)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil ibn Darraj who has said the following: “About the case of a man who buys food then sells it before receiving delivery, he (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’ ‘Can he appoint the second buyer as his agent to receive delivery?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
